rooms.name: Head Platform
rooms.description: The station sign is legible in mirror writing in the water below. A dry stair leads back to the trial weir.

changes.text: Dark water covers the rail cut and all the track beyond it.
Water drips from the uncovered rails all the way to the trim siding.

encounters.cue: Inspect the lowest row of letters on the station sign.
encounters.result: The painter repeated the name upside down on the bottom board. Boat crews could read it reflected when the rail was under water.

rooms.name: Rail Cut
rooms.description: A slice through white salt exposes a black seam of old rushes. The rail follows the seam down the bank.

encounters.cue: Examine the black seam in the salt.
encounters.result: A few stems still carry woven crossings. The rails pass above the remains of a rush mat laid on an older shore.

rooms.name: Ticket Slot
rooms.description: A metal tongue rings when a token passes through. The fare table offers a free return to every rescue worker.

encounters.cue: Look behind the tongue of the ticket slot.
encounters.result: The rescue token has left a second wear mark near the hinge. Its thicker rim made a different note as it passed.

rooms.name: Brake Drum
rooms.description: A rope wound on the drum still holds the last empty train in place. One strand is much newer than the rest.

encounters.cue: Inspect the new strand in the brake rope.
encounters.result: The splice passes under every old strand in turn. The worker renewed the rope while the wagons were still pulling on it.

rooms.name: Trim Siding
rooms.description: A wagon rests on a weighbridge. A stamped brass scale couples its axle weight to the return conduit setting.

encounters.cue: The original trim scale is riveted to the weighbridge.
encounters.result: A loaded axle balances at four teeth. The return valve needs this reading together with the three-spring survey.
encounters.hint: Draw down the lake at the trial weir to expose the scale.

rooms.name: Brine Engine
rooms.description: Salt crust has welded the wheels to the sleepers. A lunch pail hangs in the cab above the crust.

encounters.cue: Look inside the pail hanging in the cab.
encounters.result: The lid has a groove the width of a wheel flange. A driver used it as a rough gauge long after the last lunch.

rooms.name: Shunter's Box
rooms.description: Pell marks every loaded wagon with a bird's footprint. His own boots have the same three nails.

encounters.cue: Pell the shunter still stamps wagons although the timetable has faded.
encounters.result: Pell weighed an axle at the trim siding on the night of the flood. The painted number washed off, but he stamped it in brass.

rooms.name: Sleeper Stack
rooms.description: Old sleepers are cut shorter at one end. Those ends served as splints on the night of the flood.

encounters.cue: Examine the cut ends of the shortened sleepers.
encounters.result: The sharp corners were rounded before the wood was split off. Even under pressure someone took care of the skin against the splint.

rooms.name: Chalk Mile
rooms.description: A chalk face carries hand-drawn distances to a spring, a dry landing and a door marked RETURN.

encounters.cue: Compare the tails of the chalk arrows.
encounters.result: The distances are counted in laden paces. A little drawing of two boots and a stretcher explains why the marks lie so close together.

rooms.name: Load Bell
rooms.description: A rail hammered flat at one end hangs from a cable. It rings half a note below the shift bell.

encounters.cue: Inspect the hammer beside the flattened rail.
encounters.result: One face is wrapped in cord. It makes a short note a crew could tell apart from the long call across the lake.

rooms.name: Cable Saddle
rooms.description: Grease has kept the groove in the saddle bright. A hairline crack runs across the mounting block.

encounters.cue: Look at the ends of the hairline crack.
encounters.result: Tiny drilled pits stop the crack at both ends. The grease is wiped away between them so any growth would show.

rooms.name: Salt Sacks
rooms.description: The sacks have dissolved, leaving white cubes with the weave of the cloth still stamped in them.

encounters.cue: Read the weave impressed in a salt block.
encounters.result: A thick mended patch stands out among the threads. The sack had already carried several loads before the brine took the cloth.

rooms.name: Switch Fan
rooms.description: Five rails spread like fingers. Little carved arrows mark a walking route along the outermost one.

encounters.cue: Trace the arrows on the outer rail.
encounters.result: The cuts face away from the switch blades. A walker following them could keep clear of the pinch points even in poor light.

rooms.name: Ballast Pocket
rooms.description: Rounded lake pebbles fill a pocket between the rails. An old ferry fare is mixed among them.

encounters.cue: Look at the old fare among the pebbles.
encounters.result: One edge is hammered flat to the rail width. Someone used the useless fare to check a gap between the stones.

rooms.name: Ganger's Stove
rooms.description: Tea still stains the inside of the rail workers' kettle. The stove draws air through a hollow sleeper.

encounters.cue: Inspect the open end of the hollow sleeper.
encounters.result: A sieve of punched tin covers the inlet. It kept ballast out of the fire and little feet away from the draught.

rooms.name: Repair Cradle
rooms.description: The cradle lifts one wheelset at a time. A diagram on its hook shows where to read the trim scale.

encounters.cue: Read the engraving on the cradle hook.
encounters.result: The wheel is drawn with its weight entirely off the rail. A loaded axle would give the reader a different mark.

rooms.name: Whitening Arch
rooms.description: Salt blooms in long white needles on the arch. They snap under a breath and grow again with each trial.

encounters.cue: Look at the roots of the long salt needles.
encounters.result: Each grows from a tiny dark pit. Broken tips fall away, but the next tide starts a needle in exactly the same place.

rooms.name: End Buffer
rooms.description: The wooden face is split where the last wagon stopped. Someone painted a small thank-you inside the split.

encounters.cue: Read the little note inside the split.
encounters.result: A small wheel is painted beneath the thanks. The painter used the open crack as the line where the wagon finally stopped.

rooms.name: Mineral Lift
rooms.description: A counterbalanced cage links the salt workings to the kiln wagon above.

encounters.cue: Examine the counterweight pockets.
encounters.result: They take broken kiln tiles edge-on. A worker could balance a load with scraps too small to sell.

rooms.name: Seep Mouth
rooms.description: A clear thread of spring water has eaten a tunnel just high enough for a railway worker on hands and knees.

encounters.cue: Inspect the low threshold of the seep.
encounters.result: Two shallow cups have been rubbed into the stone. Crawlers set their knees there to reach the dry handhold beyond.

links.hint: Draw the lake at the trial weir.

links.obstacle: The narrow seep floods at high water.
